author: NorthEast News Desk
body: David Morales defeated incumbent Providence Mayor Brett Smiley in Wednesday’s Democratic primary, ending Smiley’s bid for a second term and positioning the 27-year-old challenger to become the city’s next mayor.

Morales identifies as a democratic socialist and received endorsements from U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna and several labor unions. He built his campaign around housing affordability, public schools and a proposal to cap rent increases.

Smiley, 47, highlighted housing construction, lower crime and the city’s return to control of Providence schools after years of state administration. The policy contrast sharpened around rent stabilization: Smiley vetoed an ordinance in April, while Morales said he would work with the City Council to pass and enforce such a measure early in his administration.

NBC 10 reported that Morales has no listed opponent for the November 3 election after Republican David Talan was no longer shown on the ballot. Barring a new ballot development, the Democratic primary victory makes Morales the presumptive next mayor of Rhode Island’s capital.
dek: The 27-year-old democratic socialist defeated incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley and has no listed opponent in November.
headline: David Morales ousts Providence Mayor Brett Smiley in Democratic primary
